name: Asa in his latter years
charge: Relying on the king of Syria and not on the Lord; putting the seer in a prison house for the rebuke; in his disease seeking not to the Lord, but to the physicians
summary: In Asa’s thirty-sixth year Baasha of Israel built Ramah to cut Judah off, and instead of crying to the Lord as he had against Zerah, Asa took silver and gold out of the house of the Lord and hired Ben-hadad of Syria to attack his brothers in the north (2 Chronicles 16:1-6). Hanani the seer rebuked him for relying on Syria and not on the Lord, and told him he would have wars from then on; Asa put the seer in prison and oppressed some of the people (2 Chronicles 16:7-10). Diseased in his feet, he sought not the Lord but the physicians, and died (2 Chronicles 16:12-13).
offenseFull: Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah so that none could go out or come in to Asa (2 Chronicles 16:1). Tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa, and Baasha was trying to stop them. This was internal beef within the nation of Israel, and there are internal battles among us still. Asa brought silver and gold out of the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of his own house and sent it to Ben-hadad king of Syria at Damascus, asking him to break his league with Baasha. Ben-hadad sent his captains against the cities of Israel, Baasha stopped building, and Asa carried off the stones of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah (2 Chronicles 16:2-6). He went into his treasury and paid the heathen to fight his brother. That is a sick mindset: rejoicing when the heathen come against your own people, even people in error, instead of hoping the Most High has mercy on them. Cursed is the man who trusts in man.

Hanani the seer came and told him that because he had relied on the king of Syria and not on the Lord, the host of Syria had escaped his hand. Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host with many chariots? Yet because he relied on the Lord, the Lord delivered them to him. The eyes of the Lord run to and fro through the whole earth to show Himself strong for those whose heart is perfect toward Him; in this he had done foolishly, and from then on he would have wars (2 Chronicles 16:7-9). God wants the glory. The help comes with conditions: the heart has to be right. Many today go to therapists, spiritual healers and lying churches instead of asking what the Bible says to do.

Then Asa was angry with the seer and put him in a prison house, for he was in a rage over it, and he oppressed some of the people at the same time (2 Chronicles 16:10). He did not ask how to get right with God; he locked up the man of God who told him the truth and took it out on everyone around him. In his thirty-ninth year he was diseased in his feet until the disease was exceeding great, as diabetics lose toes and their legs swell, yet in his disease he sought not the Lord but the physicians (2 Chronicles 16:12). Who do you seek first and foremost when you are sick? The Lord, not the physician first. The rebuke is not against physicians: honour the physician, for the Lord created him, but healing comes from the Most High, and in sickness you pray, leave off from sin and cleanse your heart, and then give place to the physician (Ecclesiasticus 38:1-2, 9-12). Job called his comforters physicians of no value (Job 13:4).
judgmentFull: The host of Syria escaped his hand, and from then on he had wars (2 Chronicles 16:7, 9). You want to know why some problems never go away: the same wrong decision keeps being made, and nothing changes in the house. He bought temporary relief and lost the greater deliverance that relying on God would have brought.

His disease grew exceeding great, and Asa slept with his fathers in the forty-first year of his reign. They buried him in the sepulchre he had made in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning (2 Chronicles 16:13-14). His acts first and last are written in the book of the kings (2 Chronicles 16:11), and they were written for our learning, so that we would have hope through the scriptures and not through a loan from the bank or a therapist (Romans 15:4). The heart of Asa was perfect all his days (2 Chronicles 15:17), yet he ended relying on Syria and on physicians with the seer in prison. The Lord is with you while you are with Him, and if you forsake Him He will forsake you (2 Chronicles 15:2).

text.text: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben–hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
And Ben–hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel–maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.
Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the Lord thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.
Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the Lord, he delivered them into thine hand.

For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time.
And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.
And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

For of the most High cometh healing, and he shall receive honour of the king.
My son, in thy sickness be not negligent: but pray unto the Lord, and he will make thee whole.
Leave off from sin, and order thine hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all wickedness.
Give a sweet savour, and a memorial of fine flour; and make a fat offering, as not being.
Then give place to the physician, for the Lord hath created him: let him not go from thee, for thou hast need of him.
But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
